revision:
ONE-ROUND REVISION — preserve the current working composition and implement these bounded changes in priority order:
1. Preserve and clarify intent: Preserve the complete board, player, two crates, two goals, controls, HUD, and objectives, but make the mechanic relationships explicit. Keep every brief-required object, label, control, state, and relationship visible inside 1280×800; do not trade compliance for a cleaner crop.
2. Establish the reading structure: Enlarge the board substantially and pull the controls and objectives closer to its left and right edges, creating one compact gameplay group rather than three distant islands. Reposition and rescale existing elements rather than deleting them; allow one primary focal region, one supporting information tier, and quiet utility controls.
3. Finish the shared system: Trim the board container precisely to the 10-column grid and establish one tile-gap, border, and inset-shadow token. Apply the correction through a small consistent set of palette, type, spacing, stroke, border, radius, shadow, and illustration rules, and repair visible clipping, collisions, weak contrast, or unfinished edges.
4. Add one content-specific expressive payoff: Give player, crates, lever, door, and targets distinct foundry-specific silhouettes and state changes, introduce purposeful floor wear and heat markings along likely routes, and create one expressive lever-to-door visual linkage while preserving board readability. Limit this to the hero and semantically different states; reuse the system tokens and remove arbitrary decoration so it does not create a second competing focal point.
Implementation guardrails: edit the existing self-contained HTML/CSS/JS; use no remote assets, libraries, fonts, APIs, canvas packages, or network calls. Keep the fixed viewport at 1280×800 with no scrolling. Preserve all functioning content and verify small text, edge safety, and component alignment after the revision.
conflicts: Completeness versus hierarchy: retain the fidelity action—Preserve the complete board, player, two crates, two goals, controls, HUD, and objectives, but make the mechanic relationships explicit.—while using the clarity action—Enlarge the board substantially and pull the controls and objectives closer to its left and right edges, creating one compact gameplay group rather than three distant islands.—to tier, group, and rescale the required material instead of removing it.

System consistency versus expression: implement the craft action—Trim the board container precisely to the 10-column grid and establish one tile-gap, border, and inset-shadow token.—as the construction grammar, then permit the expressive action—Give player, crates, lever, door, and targets distinct foundry-specific silhouettes and state changes, introduce purposeful floor wear and heat markings along likely routes, and create one expressive lever-to-door visual linkage while preserving board readability.—only as a bounded, content-motivated hero/state exception.

One-round scope versus accumulated requests: prioritize visible requirement ambiguity and the dominant craft defect first; apply secondary typography, spacing, and decorative refinements only when they reuse the same rules and do not trigger a rebuild.
rationale: The plan preserves every requested and already working element, lets hierarchy determine prominence, uses craft rules as the implementation substrate, and admits a single semantically motivated expressive exception so one revision remains coherent and feasible.
